The urban-rural temperature gap is more pronounced in arid cities because the surrounding countryside lacks moisture for evapotranspiration, stripping away the rural evaporative cooling advantage that would otherwise narrow the UHI.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If arid cities heavily irrigate their urban core, the latent heat differential may reverse.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If coastal cities experience regular nocturnal advection, regional aridity is a poor predictor of the UHI gap.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If anthropogenic heat release scales non-linearly with population, aridity becomes a secondary modulator.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"In humid regions, the rural countryside cools at night via evapotranspiration, creating a large UHI gap.
